subproblem.title: Lusin–Egorov: uniform lower density and cone bounds on a subset of almost full measure (Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6 ⇐, (4)–(9))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, M ⊆ ℝ^P Borel with Hⁿ(M) < ∞ (Hⁿ = μHE[n], μ := Hⁿ⌞M), and Q : ℝ^P → linear subspaces of ℝ^P such that x ↦ p_{Q(x)} (orthogonal projection, an element of L(ℝ^P) with the operator norm) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable and M has approximate tangent space Q(x) at μ-a.e. x. Let a, b, ε be real numbers with ofReal(a) < ωₙ = unitBallVolume n, b > 0 and ε > 0. Then there are E ⊆ M and δ > 0 such that Hⁿ(M ∖ E) < ε, dim Q(x) = n for every x ∈ E, and for all x, y ∈ E and 0 < ρ < δ: ofReal(aρⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y)) and μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(bρⁿ), where X(x) := {z : 2|p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| < |z − x|}.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (Q : Euclid P → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 0 < n → MeasurableSet M → μHE[n] M ≠ ∞ → AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => (Q x).starProjection) (μHE[n].restrict M) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict M), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x (Q x)) → ∀ (a b ε : ℝ), ENNReal.ofReal a < unitBallVolume n → 0 < b → 0 < ε → ∃ (E : Set (Euclid P)) (δ : ℝ), E ⊆ M ∧ 0 < δ ∧ μHE[n] (M \ E) < ENNReal.ofReal ε ∧ (∀ x ∈ E, Module.finrank ℝ (Q x) = n) ∧ (∀ y ∈ E, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < δ → ENNReal.ofReal (a * ρ ^ n) ≤ (μHE[n].restrict M) (closedBall y ρ)) ∧ ∀ x ∈ E, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < δ → (μHE[n].restrict M) ({z | 2 * ‖(Q x).starProjection (z - x)‖ < ‖z - x‖} ∩ ball x ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (b * ρ ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 3–5 (Lusin, Egorov, uniform density bounds); Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6 “⇐”, chapter-03.txt lines 168–219 (choice of the closed set F in (4), the densities (5)–(6), the functions f_k, q_k and (7), Egoroff's theorem (8) and the uniform bounds (9)). The parent applies this with a = (1 − ε₀)ωₙ, b = ε₀ωₙ, ε₀ = 2⁻¹16⁻ⁿ (the corrected constant). Throughout μ := Hⁿ⌞M is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P (Hⁿ(M) < ∞), and for every S ⊆ M we have μ(S) = Hⁿ(S ∩ M) = Hⁿ(S) (Mathlib `Measure.restrict_apply'`, M Borel).

1. A Borel set of good points. Since x ↦ p_{Q(x)} is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, there is a strongly measurable (Borel) g : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P) with g(x) = p_{Q(x)} for μ-a.e. x. Hence the set Z of points x ∈ M at which g(x) ≠ p_{Q(x)} or M has no approximate tangent space Q(x) at x is μ-null, so Hⁿ(Z) = μ(Z) = 0. Choose a Borel set N ⊇ Z with Hⁿ(N) = 0 (Mathlib `exists_measurable_superset_of_null`) and put M₁ := M ∖ N. Then M₁ is Borel, Hⁿ(M ∖ M₁) = 0, and every x ∈ M₁ satisfies g(x) = p_{Q(x)} and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q(x); in particular dim Q(x) = n.
2. Lusin: continuity of the plane field on a large closed set (the closed set F of Simon's (4)). L(ℝ^P) is a finite-dimensional normed space, hence second countable, and carries its Borel σ-algebra; g is measurable (being strongly measurable). Apply the sibling lusin (Lusin's theorem) to the measure μ, the Borel set A := M₁ (μ(M₁) < ∞), the map g : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P) and the tolerance ofReal(ε/3) ≠ 0: there is a compact K ⊆ M₁ with μ(M₁ ∖ K) < ε/3 on which g is continuous. Put F := K; F is compact, hence closed, F ⊆ M₁ and μ(M₁ ∖ F) < ε/3. Since g(x) = p_{Q(x)} for x ∈ F ⊆ M₁, the map x ↦ p_{Q(x)} is continuous on F in the operator norm.
3. Pointwise eventual bounds ((5), (6), (7) of the source). Let x ∈ F. By the lower density lemma (sibling lower_density, applied with c := ofReal(a) < ωₙ, n ≥ 1) there is ρ₁(x) > 0 with ofReal(a)·ofReal(ρⁿ) ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) for 0 < ρ < ρ₁(x). By the cone density lemma (sibling cone_density, applied with t := ofReal(b) > 0, using n ≥ 1 and Hⁿ(M) < ∞) there is ρ₂(x) > 0 with Hⁿ(M ∩ X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(b)·ofReal(ρⁿ) for 0 < ρ < ρ₂(x). Now ofReal(a)ofReal(ρⁿ) = ofReal(aρⁿ) if a ≥ 0, while ofReal(aρⁿ) = 0 if a < 0, and ofReal(b)ofReal(ρⁿ) = ofReal(bρⁿ). Since Hⁿ(M ∩ S) = μ(S) for Borel S, we get, for 0 < ρ < min(ρ₁(x), ρ₂(x)): ofReal(aρⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(x)) and μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(bρⁿ).
4. The sets of uniformity (the source's f_k, q_k). For k ∈ ℕ put δ_k := 1/(k + 1) and
  A_k := {y ∈ ℝ^P : ofReal(aρⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y)) for all ρ ∈ (0, δ_k)},
  C_k := {x ∈ F : μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(bρⁿ) for all ρ ∈ (0, δ_k)},
  G_k := A_k ∩ C_k ⊆ F.
 (i) A_k is closed. Fix ρ > 0, s ∈ [0, ∞) and let y_i → y with μ(B̄_ρ(y_i)) ≥ s for all i. If z ∉ B̄_ρ(y) then |z − y| > ρ, so |z − y_i| > ρ for all large i; thus the indicator of U := ℝ^P ∖ B̄_ρ(y) is ≤ liminf_i of the indicators of U_i := ℝ^P ∖ B̄_ρ(y_i) (Borel sets), and Fatou's lemma gives μ(U) ≤ liminf_i μ(U_i) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) − s. As μ is finite, μ(B̄_ρ(y)) = μ(ℝ^P) − μ(U) ≥ s. So {y : μ(B̄_ρ(y)) ≥ s} is sequentially closed, hence closed, and A_k is an intersection of such sets.
 (ii) C_k is closed. Fix ρ > 0, s ∈ [0, ∞) and let x_i ∈ F, x_i → x, with μ(X(x_i) ∩ B_ρ(x_i)) ≤ s. Then x ∈ F because F is closed. Let z ∈ X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x). By step 2, ‖p_{Q(x_i)} − p_{Q(x)}‖ → 0, hence |p_{Q(x_i)}(z − x_i) − p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| ≤ ‖p_{Q(x_i)} − p_{Q(x)}‖|z − x_i| + |x − x_i| → 0, while |z − x_i| → |z − x|; so the strict inequalities 2|p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| < |z − x| and |z − x| < ρ persist with x_i in place of x for all large i. Thus 1_{X(x)∩B_ρ(x)} ≤ liminf_i 1_{X(x_i)∩B_ρ(x_i)} pointwise; these sets are open (as X(x_i) is the preimage of an open set under a continuous map), and Fatou's lemma (Mathlib `lintegral_liminf_le`) gives μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ liminf_i μ(X(x_i) ∩ B_ρ(x_i)) ≤ s. So {x ∈ F : μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ s} is sequentially closed, hence closed, and C_k is an intersection of such sets.
 (iii) G_k ⊆ G_{k+1}, since δ_{k+1} < δ_k makes the defining conditions weaker, and ⋃_k G_k = F: for x ∈ F choose k with δ_k ≤ min(ρ₁(x), ρ₂(x)) and use step 3.
5. Egoroff step ((8) of the source). The closed (hence Borel) sets G_k increase to F, so μ(G_k) → μ(F) (Mathlib `tendsto_measure_iUnion_atTop`) and, μ being finite and G_k ⊆ F, μ(F ∖ G_k) = μ(F) − μ(G_k) → 0. Fix k with μ(F ∖ G_k) < ε/3 and set E := G_k, δ := δ_k > 0.
6. Verification ((9) of the source). E ⊆ F ⊆ M₁ ⊆ M. Every x ∈ E lies in M₁, so dim Q(x) = n. For y ∈ E ⊆ A_k and 0 < ρ < δ: ofReal(aρⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y)). For x ∈ E ⊆ C_k and 0 < ρ < δ: μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(bρⁿ). Finally M ∖ E ⊆ (M ∖ M₁) ∪ (M₁ ∖ F) ∪ (F ∖ E), all three subsets of M, so by subadditivity Hⁿ(M ∖ E) ≤ 0 + μ(M₁ ∖ F) + μ(F ∖ E) < ε/3 + ε/3 < ε. ∎
(Remark: Simon also intersects E with a large ball to make it compact; this is not needed here because the covering step of the sibling uniform_to_rectifiable uses countably many balls.)
proof_key_steps: Replace p_{Q(·)} by a Borel representative g and discard a Borel null set: M₁ ⊆ M of full measure, all points tangent with g = p_{Q(·)}.
Lusin (sibling lusin) on g : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P): compact F ⊆ M₁ with μ(M₁ ∖ F) < ε/3 and x ↦ p_{Q(x)} continuous on F.
At each x ∈ F the reused lower density lemma and the cone density lemma give the bounds for 0 < ρ < ρ(x).
A_k (closed balls, upper semicontinuity via Fatou on complements) and C_k (open cones, continuity on F + Fatou) are closed; G_k = A_k ∩ C_k increase to F.
Continuity from below: μ(F ∖ G_k) < ε/3 for some k; E := G_k, δ := 1/(k+1) satisfy all conclusions.

audit.reason: The proof correctly obtains a Borel set of good points and applies the three declared dependencies. Finite measure validates closed-ball upper semicontinuity; projection continuity and Fatou validate cone-mass lower semicontinuity. The increasing closed sets exhaust F, giving the uniform radius and required measure error, including when a is negative.
